authority: diagnostic: paper only, not investment advice
flags: Hinge Health completed the acquisition of Cylinder Health, a virtual-first digestive healthcare company. The nine-month cash flow statement shows 97,353 (table in thousands) paid for the business, net of cash acquired. Goodwill rose to 113,030 (table in thousands) from 64,096 (table in thousands) at year-end 2025.
The Board approved an increase to the share repurchase program, leaving $300.0 million available for future repurchase and a total authorization of $496.5 million.

President James Pursley notified the company he will resign as President effective at the start of 2027 and was appointed a Class II director effective in early January 2027. The 8-K says the decision was not the result of any disagreement.
no_value_reason: no valuation route yet for a company with no operating profit in 3 of its last 3 fiscal years

business_model.claim: Hinge Health sells an AI-driven digital care platform that pairs motion tracking, a wearable nerve-stimulation device and a care team. It began with joint and muscle (MSK) care and has expanded into migraine and, through the Cylinder Health acquisition, gastrointestinal care.
quotes: Hinge Health leverages software, including AI, to automate care for joint and muscle health, delivering an outstanding member experience, improved member outcomes, and cost reductions for our clients and members.

In 2026, we launched our Migraine Care Program, our first expansion beyond joint and muscle pain, offering rapid drug-free pain relief, personalized trigger management, and expert-led prevention for members.

business_model.claim: The paying customers are mainly self-insured employers, with health plans' fully-insured and Medicare Advantage populations and federal plans as additional markets. Members use the platform through these clients.
quotes: Our clients are primarily self-insured employers and include many of the nation’s leading enterprises across a broad range of industries and sizes.

business_model.claim: Most revenue is channelled through partners, mainly health plans and PBMs. Client contracts through partners were 82% of revenue in the latest fiscal year. Three large health plans each exceeded 10%: HCSC 17.5%, Elevance 13.7% and Aetna 10.5%.
quotes: Client contracts through our partners accounted for 82% of our revenue for the year ended December 31, 2025 and 79% of our revenue for the year ended December 31, 2024.

business_model.claim: Revenue comes from annual per-member subscriptions, recognized ratably over 12 months, and clients pay only for members who engage. Most clients are now billed under an engagement-based model: an upfront annual platform fee per member plus a fee per completed billable session.
quotes: We primarily recognize revenue ratably over the 12 months after an eligible life becomes a member, and as such our revenue has historically been highly predictable.
Most of our clients are billed through an engagement-based pricing model based on an annual upfront platform fee per member plus a fee per each completed billable session.

business_model.claim: Revenue growth is driven by the client base, contracted lives and member engagement. Clients rose to 3,270 from 2,560 a year earlier, and third-quarter revenue grew 52% to $235.0 million. Contracted lives were about 25 million at the last year-end disclosed.
quotes: We have rapidly grown our client base, expanding to 3,270 clients as of September 30, 2026 compared to 2,560 clients as of September 30, 2025.

business_model.claim: Billing is seasonal and runs ahead of revenue. Most new clients sign in the second half of the year and launch in the first half of the next. Billings peak in the second quarter and revenue is recognized later, so deferred revenue grew to 459,174 from 300,855 at the prior year-end (table in thousands). LTM calculated billings were $960.3 million versus $624.2 million.
quotes: The majority of new clients enter into contracts with us in the second half of each calendar year, which aligns with the typical employee benefit enrollment period.

business_model.basis: stated in the cited items; the margin trend is read from the reported figures
business_model.claim: Cost of revenue is mainly the care team, support staff, device inventory and technology costs, and it grew more slowly than revenue. Third-quarter GAAP gross margin was 87% versus 82% a year earlier.
quotes: These costs primarily include personnel-related costs, including employee salaries, stock-based compensation, and other related expenses for our care team, support operations personnel, and site reliability engineering personnel.

business_model.claim: Operating costs are led by sales and marketing (85,241 in the third quarter), followed by research and development (37,473) and general and administrative (31,291) (table in thousands). Commissions are amortized over the benefit period. Operating income was 50,325 on revenue of 234,970, a 21% GAAP operating margin.
quotes: We amortize third-party sales commissions and amortize a portion of internal sales commissions over the respective benefit periods.

business_model.basis: stated in the cited items; the link to the nine-month swing is inferred from the figures and the IPO disclosure
business_model.claim: Reported profitability is distorted by one-off stock-based compensation. Nine-month stock-based compensation was 50,324 versus 625,837 a year earlier (table in thousands). Management attributes a $571.4 million charge to the IPO vesting trigger, which explains the prior-year net loss and the swing to profit.

Contracts often include performance guarantees that put part of the fees at risk, tied to engagement thresholds, member-reported outcomes and client return on investment. The company says payouts have been immaterial so far.
quotes: We have historically paid an immaterial amount related to these performance guarantees.

business_model.basis: stated in the cited item; the link to deferred revenue is inferred from the cash flow lines
business_model.claim: The business converts to cash well because billings precede revenue. Nine-month operating cash flow was 259,098 versus 107,548 a year earlier (table in thousands), helped by a 156,741 increase in deferred revenue. The company used cash for 157,384 of share repurchases and 97,353 for a business acquisition.
